claim.pdf_says: FUNCTION SUBSTITUTE ( argument-1 { [ ANYCASE ] [ FIRST / LAST ] argument-2 argument-3 } ... )  -- printed as ONE tall square bracket enclosing FIRST stacked above LAST (verified at 300 dpi crop), i.e. a single optional choice of at most one of FIRST or LAST; no choice-indicator vertical bars are present inside either the brace or the bracket. FUNCTION, SUBSTITUTE, ANYCASE, FIRST and LAST are all underlined (required words).
claim.markdown_says:
```
FUNCTION SUBSTITUTE ( argument-1 { [ ANYCASE ] [ FIRST ] argument-2 argument-3 } ... )
                                               [ LAST  ]
```
claim.why_it_matters: The one tall stacked-alternatives bracket has been transcribed as TWO independent square brackets, one under the other. Read literally that permits both FIRST and LAST to be specified in the same argument group, which the printed diagram forbids (a bracket around stacked alternatives without choice-indicator bars means AT MOST ONE, 5.2.6.4). The transcription is also the only general format in clause 15 on these pages that uses ad-hoc two-line ASCII brackets instead of the tall-delimiter convention the rest of the file uses (e.g. 15.65.2 MODULE-NAME uses the U+23A7..U+23AD stacked delimiters plus a 'Figure notes' paragraph), and it carries no Figure notes. The required-word underlining on FUNCTION, SUBSTITUTE, ANYCASE, FIRST and LAST is also dropped, although 15.92.2 on page 955 preserves it.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED on both sides, and the meaning change is provable from the transcription file's own notation vocabulary rather than from an appeal to ISO 5.2.6.4 alone.

PDF (rendered E:/Temp/specrecon/v949/spec_p949.png at 300 dpi, then cropped to the 15.87.2 format line and enlarged 5x): the printed general format is `FUNCTION SUBSTITUTE` followed by tall literal argument parentheses containing `argument-1 { [ ANYCASE ] <bracket> argument-2 argument-3 } ...`. Reading the glyphs directly at 5x: there is exactly ONE tall square bracket after `[ ANYCASE ]` -- a single left bracket whose top and bottom serifs span BOTH text rows, and a matching single right bracket -- enclosing FIRST on the upper row and LAST on the lower row. FIRST and LAST each carry their own underline rule (the middle horizontal rule is FIRST's underline, the bottom rule is LAST's). FUNCTION, SUBSTITUTE and ANYCASE are underlined as well. I looked specifically for choice-indicator vertical bars: there are NONE anywhere in the figure -- not inside the `{ }` brace and not inside the tall bracket. So the printed notation is an optional group of stacked alternatives = at most one of FIRST or LAST.

Markdown (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 38006-38009, dumped byte-exact with `cat -A`): the fenced block is literally
  FUNCTION SUBSTITUTE ( argument-1 { [ ANYCASE ] [ FIRST ] argument-2 argument-3 } ... )$
                                                 [ LAST  ]$
Two separate ASCII bracket PAIRS, one per line. The claim quotes both sources accurately.

Adversarial test -- is the two-line ASCII form merely a formatting approximation that still reads as 'at most one'? No, and this file settles it against the transcription:
  (a) The file already uses stacked one-per-line `[ X ]` / `[ Y ]` ASCII brackets to mean INDEPENDENT, CO-OCCURRING optional clauses. Screen description entry Format 1 (lines 17085-17091 and 17148-17151) renders `[ FULL ]`, `[ AUTO ]`, `[ SECURE ]`, `[ REQUIRED ]` exactly that way, and those four clauses may all be specified together. The data-description Format 1 clause list (lines 16828-16840) does the same. So `[ FIRST ]` above `[ LAST  ]` collides with this file's established spelling for 'both are allowed'.
  (b) The file has a DIFFERENT, consistently used spelling for an optional at-most-one stacked pair: the tall U+23A1..U+23A6 delimiters. Screen attributes use `⎡ HIGHLIGHT ⎤ / ⎣ LOWLIGHT ⎦` (line 17172); the sign phrase uses `⎡ + ⎤ / ⎣ - ⎦`.
  (c) The decisive control is nine sections later on the same clause: 15.96.2 FUNCTION TRIM (lines 38499-38505) is the structurally IDENTICAL construct -- an optional stacked pair of underlined required words inside a function's argument parentheses -- and it is transcribed as `⎡ LEADING ⎤ / ⎢ ⎥ / ⎣ TRAILING ⎦` with a `> **Figure notes.**` paragraph recording 'No choice indicators in this format ... zero or one may be specified' and the underlined required words. 15.65.2 MODULE-NAME (lines 36846-36856) does the same with braces. 15.87.2 SUBSTITUTE alone does neither.
So the transcription does not merely under-render the bracket; within its own notation system it renders the WRONG constraint, and it does so where its immediate siblings render the right one. This is content, not formatting: in a general format the delimiters ARE the grammar.

Secondary defects independently confirmed: no `<u>` markup and no Figure notes paragraph, so the required-word underlining on FUNCTION, SUBSTITUTE, ANYCASE, FIRST and LAST is lost with nothing recording it (15.92.2 TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME at line 38257 does keep it via `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME</u>`; printed page 925 = PDF page 955, consistent with the 30-page offset that puts PDF 949 at printed 919). Additionally, the ad-hoc second line `[ LAST  ]` sits outside every enclosing delimiter -- the `}`, the `...` and the closing `)` appear only on line 1 -- so the lower alternative is not shown as being inside the repeating brace group at all.

One sub-claim is slightly overstated but does not affect the verdict: 'the only general format in clause 15 ... that uses ad-hoc two-line ASCII brackets' is true for these pages, but the same ad-hoc stacked-ASCII-bracket rendering appears elsewhere in clause 15 -- the NUMVAL-family argument figures at lines 36965-36977 stack `[ + ]` / `[ - ]` / `[ CR ]` / `[ DB ]` the same way for what is likewise an at-most-one group. That is a sibling instance of the same defect class, not a counterexample.

Nothing in 15.87.3/15.87.4 repairs the loss. Returned value rule 3 a)/b) says 'If FIRST is specified ... else b) If LAST is specified ...', which presumes but never states mutual exclusivity; the general format is the sole syntactic authority for it.
verdict.corrected_description: REAL, structural, as described, with two refinements. (1) The core finding stands exactly: PDF page 949 section 15.87.2 prints ONE tall square bracket spanning both rows and enclosing FIRST stacked above LAST (5x crop of the 300 dpi render: single left bracket with top and bottom serifs crossing both rows, matching single right bracket, both words underlined, and NO choice-indicator vertical bars anywhere in the figure -- neither in the `{ }` brace nor in the bracket), i.e. an optional at-most-one choice; specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 38006-38009 transcribe it as two independent ASCII bracket pairs `[ FIRST ]` / `[ LAST  ]` on consecutive lines. (2) The strongest proof that this changes meaning is internal to the transcription, not just ISO 5.2.6.4: this file uses stacked one-per-line `[ X ]` / `[ Y ]` brackets precisely for independent CO-OCCURRING optional clauses (`[ FULL ]` / `[ AUTO ]` / `[ SECURE ]` / `[ REQUIRED ]` in the screen description entry, lines 17085-17091 and 17148-17151), and reserves the tall U+23A1..U+23A6 delimiters for optional stacked ALTERNATIVES -- including the structurally identical FUNCTION TRIM format nine sections later at 15.96.2 (lines 38499-38505: `⎡ LEADING ⎤` / `⎣ TRAILING ⎦` plus a Figure notes paragraph). (3) Two further losses: the second line `[ LAST  ]` sits outside every enclosing delimiter, since the `}`, the `...` and the closing `)` appear only on line 1, so the lower alternative is not shown as being within the repeating brace group; and there is neither `<u>` markup nor a Figure notes paragraph, so the required-word underlining on FUNCTION, SUBSTITUTE, ANYCASE, FIRST and LAST is dropped with nothing recording it. Fix: render 15.87.2 in the file's tall-delimiter convention, e.g. `FUNCTION SUBSTITUTE ( argument-1 ⎧ [ ANYCASE ] ⎡ FIRST ⎤ argument-2 argument-3 ⎫ ... )` with `⎣ LAST  ⎦` on the continuation row inside the brace, and add a Figure notes paragraph stating that no choice indicators appear, that the FIRST/LAST bracket is a plain bracket (zero or one), and that FUNCTION, SUBSTITUTE, ANYCASE, FIRST and LAST are underlined required words. The same defect class should be swept for elsewhere in clause 15 -- the NUMVAL-family figures at lines 36965-36977 stack `[ + ]` / `[ - ]` / `[ CR ]` / `[ DB ]` the same ad-hoc way.
